review_notes: I read the whole target file and the relevant parts of BimoduleTensor/Basic.lean (the simp lemmas for bimoduleTensorTmul, bimoduleTensorMap_tmul, bimoduleTensorLift_tmul and tmul_smul_bimoduleTensorTmul). I also searched the Shift development for shift-related simp lemmas. The two public @[simp] lemmas, bimoduleTensorShiftIso_hom_tmul and bimoduleTensorShiftIso_inv_tmul, have sensible orientation: they rewrite to the unshifted tmul and do not compete with existing rules. I found no loop risk. The only simp-interface weakness I could support is the missing application lemmas for the private pairing maps. I did not find a supported criticism of the naturality proof, which mixes rw and simp only; I could not tell whether that is forced by the shiftObj instance unification. Nothing was compiled.

findings.declaration: shiftPair / unshiftPair (private pairing maps; used by shiftHom, unshiftHom, shiftPair_degree, unshiftPair_degree)
findings.problem: The bilinear maps `shiftPair` and `unshiftPair` are built from nested structure literals. They have no application lemma of the form `shiftPair … m n = bimoduleTensorTmul … m n`. Every consumer instead re-derives the evaluation by unfolding the definition with `simp only [shiftPair, LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk, …]`, as in `shiftPair_degree`, both side-condition proofs in `shiftHom`, `unshiftPair_degree`, and both in `unshiftHom`. That is the same unfolding script five or more times, and each use depends on the structure-literal layout. `shiftHom_tmul` and `unshiftHom_tmul` also close their goals with a bare `rfl` after `rw`, which hides the same missing evaluation rule. The pairing is not exposed to simp in its natural normal form, `bimoduleTensorTmul`.
findings.proposed_change: Add private simp lemmas next to the definitions, proved by `rfl`: `shiftPair_apply_apply : shiftPair Γ Δ Θ M N a b m n = bimoduleTensorTmul Γ Δ Θ M N m n` and `unshiftPair_apply_apply : unshiftPair Γ Δ Θ M N a b m n = bimoduleTensorTmul Γ Δ Θ (M.shiftObj a) (N.shiftObj b) m n`. Then replace each `simp only [shiftPair, LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk, tmul_smul_bimoduleTensorTmul, …]` with `simp only [shiftPair_apply_apply, tmul_smul_bimoduleTensorTmul, …]`, and likewise for `unshiftPair`. The `rw …; rfl` in `shiftHom_tmul` and `unshiftHom_tmul` can then be a plain `simp [shiftHom, shiftPair_apply_apply]`, or `rw` followed by this lemma.
findings.benefit: This puts the evaluation of the pairings in a single canonical form. The proofs no longer depend on how the structure literal is laid out, and the repeated unfolding scripts shrink to short, stable rewrites. If a pairing is later changed, only the two application lemmas need updating.
